hints: Resolve all three forces horizontally and set the sum to zero: $F\cos\alpha - 20\cos 40^\circ - 100\sin 20^\circ = 0$.
Resolve all three forces vertically and set the sum to zero: $F\sin\alpha + 20\sin 40^\circ - 100\cos 20^\circ = 0$.

Find the two components $F\cos\alpha \approx 49.52$ and $F\sin\alpha \approx 81.11$, then compute $F = \sqrt{(F\cos\alpha)^2 + (F\sin\alpha)^2}$ and $\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{F\sin\alpha}{F\cos\alpha}\right)$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium ($\sum F_x = 0$):
$$F\cos\alpha - 20\cos 40^\circ - 100\sin 20^\circ = 0$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 20\cos 40^\circ + 100\sin 20^\circ \approx 15.3209 + 34.2020 = 49.5229\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium ($\sum F_y = 0$):
$$F\sin\alpha + 20\sin 40^\circ - 100\cos 20^\circ = 0$$
$$F\sin\alpha = 100\cos 20^\circ - 20\sin 40^\circ \approx 93.9693 - 12.8558 = 81.1135\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the conditions for coplanar equilibrium:
$$\sum F_x = 0\quad\text{and}\quad\sum F_y = 0$$

Resolve the three forces in the horizontal direction (taking rightwards as positive):
- Component of force $F$: $+F\cos\alpha$
- Component of $20\text{ N}$ force: $-20\cos 40^\circ$
- Component of $100\text{ N}$ force: $-100\sin 20^\circ$
Set the horizontal sum to zero:
$$F\cos\alpha - 20\cos 40^\circ - 100\sin 20^\circ = 0$$
Rearrange to isolate $F\cos\alpha$:
$$F\cos\alpha = 20\cos 40^\circ + 100\sin 20^\circ$$
Calculate each trigonometric term:
$$20\cos 40^\circ \approx 20(0.766044) = 15.3209\text{ N}$$
$$100\sin 20^\circ \approx 100(0.342020) = 34.2020\text{ N}$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 15.3209 + 34.2020 = 49.5229\text{ N} \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Resolve the three forces in the vertical direction (taking upwards as positive):
- Component of force $F$: $+F\sin\alpha$
- Component of $20\text{ N}$ force: $+20\sin 40^\circ$
- Component of $100\text{ N}$ force: $-100\cos 20^\circ$
Set the vertical sum to zero:
$$F\sin\alpha + 20\sin 40^\circ - 100\cos 20^\circ = 0$$
Rearrange to isolate $F\sin\alpha$:
$$F\sin\alpha = 100\cos 20^\circ - 20\sin 40^\circ$$
Calculate each trigonometric term:
$$100\cos 20^\circ \approx 100(0.939693) = 93.9693\text{ N}$$
$$20\sin 40^\circ \approx 20(0.642788) = 12.8558\text{ N}$$
$$F\sin\alpha = 93.9693 - 12.8558 = 81.1135\text{ N} \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Find the magnitude of $F$ by squaring and adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:
$$F^2 = (F\cos\alpha)^2 + (F\sin\alpha)^2 = (49.5229)^2 + (81.1135)^2$$
$$(49.5229)^2 \approx 2452.518$$
$$(81.1135)^2 \approx 6579.400$$
$$F^2 = 2452.518 + 6579.400 = 9031.918$$
$$F = \sqrt{9031.918} \approx 95.0364\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $F = 95.0\text{ N}$.

Find the angle $\alpha$ by dividing Equation 2 by Equation 1:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{F\sin\alpha}{F\cos\alpha} = \frac{81.1135}{49.5229} \approx 1.637899$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}(1.637899) \approx 58.5943^\circ$$
Rounding to 1 decimal place gives $\alpha = 58.6^\circ$.
